imgui.hello_includes: imgui core (imgui, draw, tables, widgets) + built-in font atlas via io.Fonts->GetTexDataAsRGBA32, no backend, no renderer
imgui.frame_includes: NewFrame + widgets + Render into draw lists (ImDrawData), no rasterization and no backend
imgui.real_includes: imgui core + imgui_impl_glfw + imgui_impl_opengl3 + glfw (see glfw_source); exe size excludes shared glfw/GL libs on Linux and macOS
imgui.glfw_source: brew glfw, shared libglfw.3.dylib, system OpenGL framework

first_frame_real.na: glfwCreateWindow fails on GitHub macOS runners with NSGL: Failed to find a suitable pixel format (tried core 3.2 and default legacy contexts, the VM has no usable OpenGL); on the arm64 runner the attempt also hung for 30 minutes, so it is not run

notes: ImGui is an immediate-mode library that only builds draw lists, the null numbers include no GPU or rasterization work
window is 960x640 for dash; imgui culls vertex generation for rows outside the window clip rect but the widget code still runs for all 50 rows
io.IniFilename is disabled, DeltaTime fixed at 1/60, no mouse input is fed
the Value label is drawn to the right of each slider, ImGui's default
built with -std=gnu++11 -Os (frame_ms) and -O2 (frame_ms_O2) with -ffunction-sections and gc-sections; Windows links libstdc++ and libgcc statically
the real window hello uses the standard GLFW + OpenGL3 backends with swap interval 0 and READY printed after the first SwapBuffers

nuklear.hello_includes: nuklear.h implementation with default font baking (stb_truetype + ProggyClean) and atlas bake to RGBA32, nk_init_default, no renderer
nuklear.frame_includes: ui build + nk_convert into vertex/element/command buffers + draw command walk, no rasterization

stripped_bytes_hello_real.na: optional, not built: Nuklear's GLFW/SDL demo backends were skipped

first_frame_real.na: optional, not built: Nuklear has no windowing code

notes: nk_convert runs with anti-aliasing on, which is Nuklear's default demo setting and costs extra vertices
font atlas is baked once at startup (included in hello size and compile time, excluded from per-frame time)
dash row uses a 4 column row template; Nuklear sliders have no label so the Value label is not drawn
all 50 dash rows are submitted every frame; Nuklear skips drawing widgets that fall outside the window
built with -std=gnu99 -Os (frame_ms) and -O2 (frame_ms_O2) with -ffunction-sections and gc-sections

microui.hello_includes: microui.c + hello scene + command iteration, no renderer, no font (text width callback is a fixed 8px per char stub)
microui.frame_includes: ui build + command list iteration via mu_next_command, no rasterization

stripped_bytes_hello_real.na: optional, not built: microui ships only an SDL2 demo with its own atlas renderer

first_frame_real.na: optional, not built: microui has no windowing code

notes: microui has no font: the text width/height callbacks are fixed-size stubs (8px wide, 16px tall), so text measurement is cheaper than a real font
hello and dash windows use the default microui theme; sliders and checkboxes are drawn in the command list, the Value label is not drawn (mu_slider has no label)
all 50 dash rows are submitted every frame; microui clips commands to the window rect but still runs layout for hidden rows
built with -std=gnu99 -Os (frame_ms) and -O2 (frame_ms_O2) with -ffunction-sections and gc-sections

clay.hello_includes: clay.h implementation + hello layout + render command array, no renderer, no font (measure text callback is a fixed 8px per char stub)
clay.frame_includes: layout build + Clay_EndLayout render command array, no rasterization

stripped_bytes_hello_real.na: Clay is a layout library with no windowing or renderer in the core

first_frame_real.na: Clay is a layout library with no windowing or renderer in the core

notes: Clay has no input widgets: buttons, checkboxes and sliders in the scenes are plain layout boxes with text and colored rectangles, with no hover, click or drag handling
checkbox and slider state is drawn from plain arrays, there is no interaction code to measure
row labels are formatted with snprintf every frame because Clay text needs memory that outlives the layout pass
Clay has no font: the measure text callback is a fixed-size stub (8px per char)
Clay output is a command array of rectangles and text, a renderer would still have to draw it
all 50 dash rows are submitted every frame; Clay lays them all out but leaves offscreen elements out of the command array
built with -std=gnu99 -Os (frame_ms) and -O2 (frame_ms_O2) with -ffunction-sections and gc-sections
